rounds.title: Menu baseline
rounds.note: First drawing of the SDK menu panel: a group label, items with a shortcut and a submenu chevron, a disabled and a destructive item, separators, a checkbox and a radio group, plus hover, active and focus-visible on a plain and a checked item, and an open submenu trigger. The menu draws no focus ring, so the ink ring rule has nothing to override. Both variants follow mint-on-light rule a (Q99): the check and the radio dot move from --et-theme-color-primary (mint, 1.33:1 on the light panel) to --et-theme-color-ink-solid: light 5.48:1, dark unchanged 13.5:1. Fixed numbers: item text 17.93:1 light, 17.18:1 dark; group label and shortcut 7.81:1 light, 6.94:1 dark; shortcut on the hover fill 6.73:1 light, 5.71:1 dark; separator 1.26:1 light, 1.73:1 dark; disabled text 2.55:1 light, 3.67:1 dark (exempt). Pane edges stay as today (Q98). Keyboard focus on an item is only the hover fill today. Variant b applies a decided rule, not a new call: a keyboard-active option gets the ink focus outline, different from hover (Q88, as the tree row in Q70). Variant a shows today for comparison.

a.note: Today: focus-visible draws the same 12 % interaction fill as hover. Light 238 on 255, 1.16:1; dark 40 on 23, 1.22:1 (pressed: 1.28:1 and 1.40:1). Under the 3:1 WCAG 1.4.11 asks of a focus indicator, and a keyboard user cannot tell focus from hover.

b.note: Pick, by the decided rule Q88. focus-visible adds a 2px inset outline in --et-theme-color-ink-solid on top of the fill: light 5.48:1 against the panel, 4.73:1 against the fill; dark 13.5:1 and 11.11:1. Hover keeps the plain fill, so focus and hover now differ, with the same ink token as every other focus ring in the SDK.
